baseline_requirements: The product targets 15 to 35 year olds.
Power source is unsettled: non-rechargeable batteries (agreed at the last meeting) versus a hybrid design with a kinetic generator as main power and a battery as backup.
The remote must include a standard battery even when an alternative power source is used.
Include a really good battery so users do not have to recharge the remote every few days.
The remote is small and slim, comfortable to hold and shaped to sit well in the hand, but not so small that it feels like a toy phone.
The product ignores teletext and all functions except controlling the TV.
The remote keeps a numeric keypad with a channel button so users can skip large numbers of channels quickly.
Jog dial function is unsettled: one view has it scrolling through stations, another has it used for volume and brightness but not channel selection.
The jog dial is flat and spun rather than raised, placed to fit the case shape and usable by both left-handed and right-handed users.
Only basic controls are visible on the front; less frequently used functions are hidden inside the snowman shape or behind a cover.
Buttons are large and easy and comfortable to press, not tiny.
Volume up and volume down buttons are clearly distinguishable and not labelled with the same symbol.
The stand-by button is red, and button colour coding is consistent across controls.
Buttons are flush with the case, with no big protruding rubber buttons.
Materials feel soft, spongy and friendly to handle, including soft rubber buttons and heavily textured plastic.
Buttons are illuminated and light up when touched, picked up or pressed, so the remote can be found and used in the dark.
The case is slightly transparent and tinted yellow, with one or two strategically placed low-power lights inside giving a subtle glow.
The remote uses a bright, non-dark colour so it is easy to find and less likely to be lost.
The product uses vibrant, natural colours.
The remote has a yellow background colour with a bold contrasting colour for the buttons.
The product incorporates the corporate colour and slogan.
The slogan is displayed on the remote, on the casing at the side.
The remote carries a company logo, and there is enough space on the design for it.
The remote is shaped like a snowman: a larger lower section that sits in the hand, with a smaller bubble on top for other functions.
The remote is not boxy, rectangular or a big square block.
The remote is not a literal fruit shape: it is not shaped like a lemon or apple, though a curvy form may take a fruit-like texture and colour.
Whether the remote can be curved is unsettled: one statement says it cannot be curved (and wood cannot be curved), while the snowman and curvy shape ideas are curved.
A titanium case must be square and cannot be curved.
A rubber case cannot include solar panels as a power source.
The housing is plastic with rubber on the outside for a warmer, more comfortable feel; the case can be plastic or rubber.
The product does not have a hard, glassy, glossy finish like the Mac iPod.

The product has a distinctive, innovative, cutting-edge look and feel achieved through design technology and style rather than extra functional features; style is the top priority for the target market.
The design avoids looking tacky.
Ease of use must be ensured throughout the product.
The design uses a unifying theme across shape, materials and colours, similar to a marketing identity, with a lemon or lime green colour suggested; the theme is to be agreed later.
Customers could buy the control with interchangeable covers in different designs.
The remote has no talk-back feature and does not speak to the user.
If voice activation is included, there is always a manual button as an alternative, possibly hidden in the opened section.
The remote has no LCD display.
baseline_decisions: Presentations will go in the order Andrew, Craig, then David.
All discussion will be held at the end of the meeting, after the presentations.
The final objective of the meeting is to reach a decision on the product concepts.
The team will take the style ideas into production, considering shape, materials and a unifying theme or series.
The team will continue with the current agenda and discuss the colour question after the other items.
The team will return to the marketing ideas first, including the fruit and vegetable concept and the corporate colour, before deciding product concepts.
Time to market is a problem, so fewer and simpler components are preferred to shorten development.
Fewer and simpler components reduce cost and complexity, so the component count should be kept low.
